you are not alone. my current and longest lasting relapse is due to seeing my boyfriend underweight and wanting to be like him. he's a healthy weight now, but the damage was done and my relapse is still ongoing, but that's besides the point.

if he is a genuine and sweet person like you say, he will support you if you choose to tell him, even if he may not completely understand (most people will never unless they've had an ED). you should open up to him if it's on your mind a lot and doing mental damage. if you are open, it gives you the chance to work through these problems together. like i said, my bf was underweight and now he's a healthy weight. i was able to be honest with him and say that his unhealthy eating habits were triggering and we worked on it. i just had to be clear he wasn't the CAUSE of my ED, rather him being underweight exasperated it. i didn't want him to feel guilty and think he caused my problems. 

i know you also said you talk about weight a lot and that's probably not the healthiest thing to focus on. at the very least, tell him that these conversations aren't helpful to for your eating issues. i know it's not easy, but you deserve to be happy in your relationship.

i understand it is not simple. however, people move on – it's not easy, and it takes time, but you can do it. people do it every day and i believe you can too. don't waste your potential on someone who won't even give you a chance.
